claims.claim: The registered decision for the playback comparison is 'no difference within the budget': for the full-recipe pair the rotation lag at the end of the manipulation window averaged 68.1 degrees with 1.67x playback and 72.7 degrees at real time, a difference of -4.6 degrees.

The effect threshold E of 139.3 degrees was driven by the 1M real-time arm, whose lag varied by 69.7 degrees across its last three checkpoints, while the two full-recipe arms varied by 6.2 and 6.4 degrees.
If E were computed only from the full-recipe arms' variation, it would be 15 degrees, and the full-recipe difference of 4.6 degrees would still be below half of it, so the decision would be the same.
In the full-recipe pair the lag accrued during the start phase of the rotation was essentially the same at 1.67x playback (77.1 degrees) and at real time (77.6 degrees).

The plan predicted that if starting the rotation needs a fixed amount of wall time, the start-phase lag would fall to about 45 degrees at real time, but the observed full-recipe real-time start-phase lag stayed at about 78 degrees.
Against its own real-time do-nothing baseline of 0.470, the full-recipe real-time policy passed the Day 1 criteria with chord_sr 0.809, maniptrans_sr 0.887 and ADD-AUC 0.547.
The full-recipe policy trained with 1.67x playback had ADD-AUC 0.431, below its do-nothing baseline of 0.471, and maniptrans_sr of about 0.0005.

Relative to each arm's do-nothing baseline, the full-recipe real-time policy did better than the 1.67x policy in the manipulation segment and in the segment after it, but worse in the segment before the manipulation.
The 1M real-time arm had no successful worlds at any of its last three checkpoints.
The full-recipe real-time arm met the registered health condition, with a manipulation-segment palm error of 4.5 cm, and the registered convergence condition.
The full-recipe real-time policy was evaluated on 4096 worlds.
The registered decision of the playback comparison is that real-time playback is better.
